Handling

Handle with care.

Before you start

Check before every use

  • Look for swelling or puffing, dents, punctures, or torn or split wrapping
  • Check the leads and connector for fraying, exposed wire or melted plastic
  • Don’t use a battery that feels hot

Be careful

Avoid short circuits

  • Never let the positive and negative touch each other or anything metal
  • Cover exposed terminals or connectors when the battery isn’t in use
  • Don’t carry loose batteries in a pocket or bag with metal items.
  • Check the polarity (+ to +, − to −) before you plug in. Connecting it backwards can damage the battery and your electronics.

In your build

Using it in your project

  • Unplug the battery before working on your wiring
  • Unplug it before soldering, and keep it away from soldering irons, heat guns and hot glue guns.
  • Don’t pull a battery out by its wires. Grip the connector.
  • Don’t draw more current than the battery is rated for.
  • Don’t run a LiPo completely flat (below about 3.0 V per cell). A low-voltage alarm helps with this.
  • Keep batteries away from water and other liquids.

Charging

Charge it right.

Battery hot, puffing or smoking?Tap for emergency steps ›

Charging station

How to use the charger

A LiPo charging station can be found at the Kirby and Electrical Makerspaces.

Know your battery

A LiPo has two connectors attached to it, a balance plug, and a discharge plug. The balance plug is only used for charging and voltage monitoring with a LiPo alarm, DO NOT power anything from the balance plug.

The LiPo supplied with the electronics kit is made from 3 cells which is known as a 3s battery. At full charge a 3s LiPo will output 12.6v and is considered flat when the battery reaches a voltage of 11v. Once the battery reaches an overall voltage of 11v it should be charged to full before the next use.

1

Connect the battery

Connect the battery to one of the ports on the charger. Make sure the balance plug is in the correct orientation and connected to the port with the (-) symbol.

NEVER pull the plugs by the wires, ALWAYS use the plastic connectors when connecting and removing plugs.
2

Select a channel

The chargers provided have two channels which allows them to charge two batteries at once. Before charging a battery, you need to select the channel you wish to charge on.

To change channels, press the CH button on the left side of the charger. Check the text in the top left to see which channel is currently selected when not on the home screen.

3

Open the settings

Press the red scroll wheel to bring up the settings for the selected channel. Use the scroll wheel to move up and down the settings. Press the red scroll wheel in to change the selected setting.

4

Check every setting

  • Selected Task: Operation to be performed by charger (Charge, Discharge, Storage)
  • Battery Type: Type of Battery to be charged (LiPo, LiIon, NiMH)
  • Cell voltage: DO NOT CHANGE
  • Cell count: Will automatically be detected and set by the charger
  • Current setting: (IMPORTANT) Set to 1C* of current battery otherwise the battery could explode

*1C = (battery capacity)/1000, e.g. 2200 mAh = 2.2A = 1C

5

Start the task and stay with it

Before pressing Start task, ensure settings are correct for the battery being charged. If not, the battery could explode while charging. If unsure at any stage, ask a staff member for assistance.

While charging there MUST be at least one member of the team within arm’s reach of the charger, NEVER CHARGE UNSUPERVISED.
6

Finish

Once the charger has finished the current task it should turn green or blue signifying the operation has finished. At this stage it is safe to remove. Always pull by the plugs instead of the cables.

Cancel a task

At any stage if you need to cancel a task, navigate to the channel, press in the scroll wheel, and select stop. Always pull by the plugs instead of the cables. Do not remove the battery without pressing stop.

Storage mode

If a LiPo battery isn’t going to be used again within 5 days, it must be charged to a storage voltage. In the settings menu select task “Storage”. This is still considered charging a battery, so all of the safety rules still apply.

Safety

Charging safety rules

Inspect before you charge.

Don’t charge a battery that is puffy, dented, punctured, or has exposed wire. Tell staff instead.

Charge at the designated station only.

Use the charging station at the Kirby or Electrical Makerspace.

Never charge unsupervised.

Someone from your team must stay within arm’s reach the whole time.

Handle plugs by the plastic connector, never the wires.

This applies when plugging in and when removing.

Know the warning signs.

If the battery gets hot, puffs up, smokes, or sizzles or pops, act immediately.

Store it safely.

If you won’t use the battery within 5 days, charge it to storage voltage and keep it alone in its fireproof bag.

Emergency

If something goes wrong:

  1. Stop the charger.
  2. Seal the battery in the LiPo-safe bag.
  3. Place it in the sand bucket and move it outdoors, away from people.
  4. Notify staff.
  5. Never use water on the battery.

Storage

Storage and Damaged Battery Management

Common causes of thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries include mechanical impact, overcharging, and exposure to external heat sources.

Environment

Batteries should be in a cool, well ventilated, dry environment, that is out of direct sunlight

Separation

Lithium batteries should be kept separated from each other and should be stored away from entry/exit ways

Storage voltage

If a LiPo battery isn’t going to be used again within 5 days, it must be charged to a storage voltage (in the settings menu for charging, select ‘Storage’; see the Charging page for more information)

Transport

While in transport, store the batteries safely, away from any sharp objects which could damage them

Damaged battery

If the battery starts doing any of the following:

  • Getting hot
  • Puffing up
  • Starting to smoke
  • Makes a sizzling sound

seal the battery in the LiPo safety bag (Figure 1, below) and place it in the bucket of sand next to the charging station (Figure 2, below). Move the bucket to an outside open dry space with nothing around it. While monitoring the battery make sure no one comes near it. Notify relevant staff and do not approach the battery.

If you have any further questions about storage or damaged battery management, please ask the staff.

Disposal

Throwing away your battery?

Is your battery visibly damaged?

No

  1. What type of battery are you using? Lithium, NiMH or alkaline
  2. Have you taped off the end terminal?
  3. Use the provided battery bins to throw away your battery!

Yes

Don’t put it in the bin. Notify makerspace staff.

  • Alkaline (AA, AAA, 9V)

How to use it:

  1. Tape the terminals
  2. Sort your battery and drop it gently into the matching slot
Swollen or damaged battery? Don’t put it in the bin. Ask staff, who will place it in the Bat-Safe box.

Types

GET TO KNOW YOUR BATTERIES

Lithium, NiMH and Alkaline

Lithium batteries

As they age, changes in their internal materials can affect their performance and potentially the risk of failure

  • Thermal runaway is the biggest issue that Lithium battery could cause: can be triggered by factors such as internal short circuits, overcharging, or excessive temperatures.

Alkaline

Alkaline batteries can overheat and build up internal gas pressure when exposed to high temperatures or short circuits, potentially causing leakage or rupture.

ALKALINE BATTERIES CAN’T BE CHARGED. DISPOSE THE DEAD ALKALINE BATTERY.
